correctness.rationale: A longest-repeat union bound gives an exponentially small exceptional set; on its complement the total complexity has Hamming Lipschitz constant ell(ell+1)/2; a clamped McShane extension plus bounded differences gives the finite-sample tail and variance bound. The endpoint Lipschitz lemma was also exhaustively checked on all binary strings through length seven.

originality.rationale: The 2004 average-sequence-complexity paper explicitly leaves asymptotic variance open, fixed-length subword papers do not control the total covariance sum, and the 2026 source paper again asks for concentration via variance. Targeted searches did not locate the finite-sample total-complexity concentration inequality or the O(n log^4 n) variance bound. Older random-trie and suffix-tree literature remains a residual risk, so the claim is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result partially resolves a long-standing concentration question, placing random total substring complexity within sqrt(n) log^2 n of its mean and allowing the sharp known mean expansion to be transferred to individual random strings with o(n) stochastic error.
